text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: CobaltFin (private VPC) - customer-reported egress failures to our model endpoints and CDN. Auto-page on-call. Severity: P1.

alice.m: on it — acknowledging page. what's the customer impact?

carla_support: CobaltFin says API calls from their VPC to hosted models 10.4.x.x are timing out. Some requests 502, some 504. They report ~30% error rate across dedicated pool instances.

bob.s: pulling logs from the dedicated pool that serves cobaltfin-tenant. quick grep shows repeated TLS handshake timeouts and connection resets to 10.4.8.21:443 (model-hosting nlb).

bob.s: snippet:```
2026-03-15T07:41:02Z  ERR  conn reset by peer: 10.4.8.21:443 -> 10.2.0.15:52344
2026-03-15T07:41:03Z  WARN healthcheck failed: nlb/health 503
```

dmitri_net: any recent SG or route changes on CobaltFin side?

carla_support: They mentioned they pushed a security group tighten yesterday evening to block outbound 0.0.0.0/0 except to whitelisted CDNs. Could be related.

alice.m: OK — hypothesis: SG rules on tenant VPC are blocking NLB health checks or NAT egress addresses, causing connection reset and TLS failures. We need to confirm whether source NAT changed and whether NLB health checks come from unexpected IPs.

tia_oncall: I can reach out to customer to get mapping of their last change and request current SG rules. Carla, please ask for the AWS console snapshot of the outbound rules and current NATGW metrics.

carla_support: pinged them and asked for SG JSON and NAT metrics. They replied with SG JSON, attaching allowed CIDRs. They only allow outbound to 13.224.0.0/14 and 34.192.0.0/12 (their CDN), nothing to our model NLB range (10.4.0.0/16).

dmitri_net: that matches. Their SG is preventing egress to our NLB private IPs. but why did it start failing now? Two thoughts: 1) we rotated model NLB to a new subnet/ip (recent deploy), 2) customer NAT/GW conntrack saturated so some traffic took different path that looks like different source IP and got blocked. need both checks.

ops-manager: deploy-bot shows a canary/scale event at 06:55 UTC that moved some backends into 10.4.8.x. not a rollback.

alice.m: mitigation plan (short term): 1) ask customer to temporarily allow outbound to our model NLB CIDR 10.4.0.0/16 (or specific ip 10.4.8.21) OR add a dedicated egress permit for the model endpoints. 2) route traffic to fallback region via DNS weight shift while customer applies SG change. 3) engineering to check conntrack on customer's NATGW if we suspect saturation.

carla_support: CobaltFin agreed to add a temporary egress rule permitting 10.4.8.21/32 for 30 minutes. they're going to apply and report back. ETA ~ 10 minutes.

bob.s: while that happens i'll prepare a fast DNS weight shift to point cobaltfin's tenant alias to regional fallback nlb at nlb-eu-west-1-02 (no IP change on their SG?). we need DNS TTL check first.

dmitri_net: also check AWS ALB/NLB healthcheck source IP ranges: health checks may originate from AWS infrastructure IPs, not the customer's VPC. but if their SG only allows to certain public ranges, internal private NLB IPs will be blocked. Confirm whether the model NLB is internal-only (it is).

tia_oncall: customer confirms the NLB is internal and they only allow outbound to public CDNs. they missed that internal NLB endpoints need explicit permission. applying the rule now.

carla_support: update: rule applied. quick test?

alice.m: running a smoke test against tenant route:```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" https://cobaltfin.tenant.api/models/text-generation -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' --connect-timeout 5 -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"
```

bob.s: returned 200. latency 180ms. errors drop to 0 over the last 2 minutes.

carla_support: customer reports requests are succeeding again. they will keep the temp rule while we validate for 30 minutes and then either keep a permanent rule or we provide alternative (private egress config).

dmitri_net: follow-ups: 1) confirm why IP change occurred — correlated with the canary/scale event. 2) recommend that customer add a CIDR permit for the entire model NLB subnet (10.4.0.0/16) for stability or implement a NAT that talks to model endpoints via a fixed egress IP. 3) consider updating our docs to include a short guidance for private VPC customers about internal NLB allowlist requirements.

ops-manager: action items assigned: alice.m -> coordinate with infra to confirm NLB rotation details; dmitri_net -> draft customer-facing recommended SG snippet; carla_support -> coordinate rollout of permanent rule and confirm security approval; tia_oncall -> monitor for 60 mins and escalate if reoccurs.

alice.m: starting investigation into the canary logs and routing table changes. attaching quick notes:```
- 06:55 UTC: autoscale event + instance drain + reconverge -> new backend IPs: 10.4.8.18-22
- 06:56 UTC: healthcheck failures spike for cobaltfin pool
- 07:03 UTC: customer applied SG tightens yesterday 22:10 local time -> conflict exposed by new backend IPs
```

bob.s: while permanent solution is decided, I'll set a brief monitor on the dedicated pool to alert if >5% errors in 5m window and page oncall.

carla_support: CobaltFin asked if Redwood can offer a single-static-egress option for private deployments so they don't manage wide SG ranges. they're open to guidance.

dmitri_net: noted. that's a product ask (private egress/exported IP). we'll file a ticket but not during P1.

tia_oncall: 30m check-in: metrics look stable, errors <0.5%. customer will review with security and likely add a /28 to allow model NLB.

ops-manager: moving to post-incident: create a short incident summary for CobaltFin and internal RCA focusing on "expectation mismatch: internal NLB IPs require explicit allowlisting when customers tighten outbound SGs; model backend rotation can surface missing allowlists".

alice.m: thanks team. closing P1 after watch period. I'll post formal RCA and customer note in #postmortems and notify account team. ✅

deploy-bot: Deployment events during incident: scale + canary at 06:55 UTC affecting cobaltfin-dedicated-pool (ids: dp-8765).

carla_support: customer message to be shared: "Thanks Redwood team — temporary rule fixed traffic. we'll add permanent /28 after security review."

alice.m: final note: recommend docs update + add a short checklist for customers doing SG hardening. I'll open a docs PR.
